coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Official school page https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/coaches/2023 ("2023 Football Coaching Staff") — still live; I also confirmed it against the site's own API (https://mgoblue.com/api/v2/Staff/coaches?$pageIndex=1&$pageSize=200&sportId=4&seasonId=47, seasonId 47 = 2023), which returns exactly the same 12 people and nothing more. That official page covers only the 11 on-field coaches plus the strength director. (2) Wikipedia's 2023 team page roster footer ("Head coach" / "Coordinators/assistant coaches" / "Support staff" navbox), which adds Jack Harbaugh and 11 named support staff. (3) Touch the Banner's "2023 Michigan Football Staff" post (Feb 17, 2023), which adds the graduate assistants, the assistant S&C coaches, and the recruiting/personnel department. (4) Wikipedia's sign-stealing scandal article for the two documented mid-season departures.

QUOTE MECHANICS. mgoblue's 2023 coaches page is a two-column Name/Title table, so name and title are NOT contiguous in the page text; for those rows the mgoblue quote is the title cell only, and a Wikipedia or Touch the Banner quote carrying name+role together is included as a second source. Wikipedia and Touch the Banner quotes are exact contiguous substrings of the rendered page text (verified by byte-level string match against the fetched HTML). On Touch the Banner, names carry trailing markers in the source ("*" = former Michigan player, "#" = hired after the 2022 season); my quotes stop before those markers.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT. This list is almost certainly incomplete on the operations/medical/equipment/video side. Michigan's athletics-wide staff directory is the only place those people are listed, and it is not recoverable for the title date: the Jan 9, 2024 Wayback capture of mgoblue.com/staff-directory is a JavaScript shell, its printable variant (mgoblue.com/staff-directory/print, captured 20240109072510) contains no staff data, and only page 1 of the backing API (10 of 241 entries, alphabetically in Administration/Baseball/Cheer) was archived — the football pages were never captured, and paged API URLs are not in the Wayback index. The 2023 Michigan Football Guide on mgoblue.com is published as topical PDF sections (player bios, season in review, record book, bowl history, etc.) with no coaches/staff section, and the CFP National Championship game notes PDF (20240103-fbl-notes-washington.pdf, 62 pages) contains no staff directory. As a result I have ZERO documented entries for: athletic trainers, team physicians, equipment managers, video/creative staff, performance nutrition, and the director of football operations. I saw a search-result assertion that Erin Zernechel was director of football operations and that Sonny Anderson was equipment manager, but I could not verify either against a 2023-dated primary page, so I did not include them. I also found no quality-control (qc) titles documented for 2023.

TIMING CAVEATS. The Touch the Banner post is dated Feb 17, 2023, i.e. the start of the 2023 cycle. Wikipedia's season navbox independently corroborates 11 of the off-field names, but for the graduate assistants, the four assistant S&C coaches, and the recruiting/personnel staff I could not independently verify each person was still employed on Jan 8, 2024; they are included as documented 2023-season staff. Two departures ARE documented and are flagged: Connor Stalions resigned Nov 3, 2023 and Chris Partridge was fired Nov 17, 2023 — neither was on staff at the championship game, and Rick Minter took over linebackers for the rest of the season. Note Wikipedia's navbox says Partridge was "fired Nov. 7," which conflicts with contemporaneous reporting and with Wikipedia's own scandal article; I used Nov 17, 2023. Jim Harbaugh served suspensions covering games 1–3 and 10–12 but was head coach at the championship game, so he carries no midseason_note. Ben Herbert is listed under his official mgoblue title (Director of Strength and Conditioning); Wikipedia records his August 2023 promotion to associate head coach, which is why his two source quotes word the role differently. Jack Harbaugh's "assistant head coach" title is categorized as "other" rather than "onfield" because he was neither a coordinator nor a position coach.
